findings.title: File and folder naming convention
findings.evidence: The repository contains the required root `README.md`, and the pipeline/data filenames follow the allowed CamelCase/date-suffix pattern: `FilingTracker_Pipeline/01_CheckUpcomingDeadlines.py`, `data/RegulatoryFilingDeadlines_20240901.csv`, and `data/UpcomingFilingAlerts_20240901.csv`. findings.title: Data quality validation present
findings.evidence: `FilingTracker_Pipeline/01_CheckUpcomingDeadlines.py` loads the CSV and performs explicit data validation before use: it asserts non-null `deadline_date` values and checks for duplicate `filing_id` rows before computing `days_until_due` and writing alerts. That satisfies the repository-level requirement for data quality validation.

findings.title: No hardcoded secrets or credentials
findings.evidence: No hardcoded secrets or credentials are present anywhere in the repository. `requirements.txt`, `README.md`, `azure-pipelines.yml`, and `FilingTracker_Pipeline/01_CheckUpcomingDeadlines.py` contain no API keys, passwords, tokens, or embedded connection strings.

findings.title: Medallion architecture (Bronze / Silver / Gold)
findings.evidence: The repository does not reference bronze/silver/gold, raw/cleansed/curated, landing/refined/reporting, or any equivalent tiered storage paths or schemas in the code or documentation. `FilingTracker_Pipeline/01_CheckUpcomingDeadlines.py` reads from `data/RegulatoryFilingDeadlines_20240901.csv` and writes to `data/UpcomingFilingAlerts_20240901.csv` without any medallion-layer paths, so medallion ordering cannot be violated here.

findings.title: Reproducibility
findings.evidence: `requirements.txt` pins dependencies (`pandas==2.1.4`, `python-dateutil==2.9.0`), satisfying reproducibility for dependency versions. The processing script `FilingTracker_Pipeline/01_CheckUpcomingDeadlines.py` is deterministic and does not introduce randomness, so no seed is required there.
